title: U.S. House · Georgia's 1st Congressional District
area: Southeast Georgia, including Savannah and the coastal counties.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Earl "Buddy" Carter (R) retired from the seat to run for U.S. Senate, finishing third in the May 19 Republican Senate primary. Amanda Hollowell won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary runoff over Joyce Marie Griggs after leading Democratic candidates was decided in an eight-way May 19 primary; James Kingston won the Republican primary outright with 52.4% of the vote.

candidates.name: Amanda Hollowell
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary runoff over Joyce Marie Griggs, 53.0% to 47.0%.

summary.text: Amanda Hollowell is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's open 1st Congressional District. A political organizer based in Savannah, she is Chief of Campaigns at Color Of Change and previously directed national organizing at When We All Vote and led advocacy campaigns at the Georgia Budget and Policy Institute and 9to5 Georgia. She won the Democratic runoff on June 16, 2026, and describes her priorities as fully funded schools, affordable healthcare, higher wages, affordable housing, climate resilience and a stronger democracy.

background.text: Born in Palm Springs, California, and graduated from Palm Springs High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Berkeley, in 2001.

Serves as Chief of Campaigns at Color Of Change, which she describes as the nation's largest online racial justice organization, where she says she leads campaigns on voting rights, economic justice and corporate accountability.
Previously directed national organizing at When We All Vote and led advocacy campaigns at the Georgia Budget and Policy Institute and 9to5 Georgia.

In Savannah, has served on the Black Heritage Festival Committee for more than a decade and on the boards of Reform Georgia, the League of Women Voters of Coastal Georgia and the Georgia Alliance for Social Justice; she is a member of The Links, Incorporated, and a graduate of the Georgia WIN List Leadership Academy, according to her Ballotpedia survey response.
Won the Democratic primary runoff for the open seat on June 16, 2026, defeating Joyce Marie Griggs, 53.0% to 47.0%.
Describes herself as a mother and the full-time caregiver to her veteran father.

priorities.text: Says she will fight to raise wages, expand affordable housing, and direct federal resources into Southeast Georgia.
priorities.quote: Families are being priced out by rising housing costs, low wages, and lack of investment in our communities. I will fight to raise wages, expand affordable housing, and ensure federal resources flow directly into Southeast Georgia.

priorities.text: Says she will work to fully fund public schools, expand universal pre-K, and strengthen apprenticeships and workforce development.
Says she will work to expand Medicaid and lower out-of-pocket healthcare costs for families, seniors, and veterans.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to expand Medicaid and lower out-of-pocket costs so healthcare is affordable and accessible for every family in the district.
positions.quote: I will fight to expand Medicaid, strengthen veteran services, and lower out-of-pocket costs so healthcare is affordable and accessible for every family in Southeast Georgia.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she supports banning assault weapons and other high-caliber weapons, and Ethan's Law.
positions.quote: She supports common-sense gun legislation like Ethan’s Law and banning assault weapons and other high-caliber weapons.

positions.summary: Her affordability agenda proposes taxing oil company profits and refunding consumers.
positions.quote: Tax excessive oil company profits and refund consumers

statements.quote: Amanda will defend LGBTQ+ rights, fight for reproductive freedom, and oppose extremist attacks on personal privacy, public health, and identity.
Amanda will champion federal investment in flood protection, resilient infrastructure, and clean energy job creation.
Increase the supply of affordable housing

candidates.name: James Kingston
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary outright with 52.4% of the vote over Patrick Farrell, Kandiss Taylor, Brian Montgomery, Eugene Yu, and Krista Penn.

summary.text: James "Jim" Kingston is the Republican nominee for Georgia's open 1st Congressional District and a first-time candidate. He is the son of former U.S. Rep. Jack Kingston, who held the seat from 1993 to 2015, and has worked in the insurance industry since 2015. He won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with an endorsement from President Trump and, according to his campaign website, is running on a conservative platform.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he grew up in Southeast Georgia near Savannah, in a family that included his siblings and his father, who represented the district in Congress.
The Current GA reports that he is the son of former Congressman Jack Kingston, and that he worked on his father's 2014 U.S. Senate campaign.
The Current GA reports that he attended the University of Georgia from 2009 to 2015 and did not earn a degree, which his campaign manager confirmed.

Has worked in the insurance industry since 2015, according to The Current GA, first at a Partners risk firm and from 2019 at Ironwood Insurance Service; his campaign website describes his work with families, small businesses and community leaders across the state.
Has not previously held elected or appointed office; this is his first campaign.

Endorsed by President Trump (per his campaign website); won the six-candidate Republican primary on May 19, 2026, defeating five other candidates and advancing to the general election without a runoff, according to WTOC. Ballotpedia lists him as the Republican nominee.

priorities.text: Says he is committed to helping President Trump "finish what he started" in Washington.
priorities.quote: Jim is committed to helping President Trump finish what he started and push back against the chaos coming out of Washington.

priorities.text: Says he wants to bring down costs for families and protect the region's military bases, port, and farms.
Says he wants to cut taxes and rein in federal spending, calling for smaller, more focused government.
priorities.quote: Washington wastes too much and takes too much. Jim believes government should be smaller, focused, and respectful of the people paying the bills.

positions.summary: Says he is pro-life and supports banning late-term abortions and ending taxpayer funding for abortion providers.
positions.quote: I am proudly pro-life and I believe it is our moral responsibility to defend the sanctity of life.

positions.summary: Says he will oppose attempts at gun control.
positions.quote: As a proud gun owner, I will oppose any attempt by radical gun control advocates to trample on our most fundamental right to protect our families, our property and our freedom.

positions.summary: Says he supports more resources for border enforcement.
positions.quote: I support deploying more resources for border enforcement to crack down on cartels and traffickers

positions.summary: Says he supports the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
positions.quote: I support the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

candidates.researchNotes: James Kingston has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and his Ballotpedia page has no biography section; background and priorities above are drawn from his campaign website (jimkingston.org), which was reachable. His campaign's Platform page returned a 404 at the time of research, so no issue-by-issue positions could be sourced to a specific ISSUES statement.

statements.quote: I proudly back the blue, oppose dangerous soft-on-crime policies and support giving our law enforcement agencies the resources they need to keep our communities safe.
I will fight for trade deals that put American workers, farmers and manufacturers first.
I will always fight to lower taxes across the board so families keep more of what they earn, and small businesses can thrive.
I support work requirements for able-bodied adults and no Medicaid handouts to illegal aliens.
I support more domestic drilling (responsibly), streamlined permitting and an all-of-the-above strategy to keep gas and electricity affordable while cutting off our reliance on foreign adversaries.

candidates.name: Dylan Castillo
candidates.ballotNote: Running on the Socialist Labor Party line.

summary.text: Dylan Castillo is a U.S. Navy veteran and environmental specialist who sought Georgia's 1st Congressional District on the Socialist Labor Party line. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a non-career politician who works to cover his bills, and lists making health care more available and less costly and rejecting corporate donations as priorities. Ballotpedia lists him as a candidate who did not make the general-election ballot.

background.text: Served on active duty in the U.S. Navy from 2014 to 2018.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Georgia Southern University in 2022.
Works as an environmental specialist; describes himself as someone who works 40 or more hours a week and is not a career politician.

priorities.text: Says he will not take money from corporate interests and campaigns on making healthcare more available and affordable.
Says he wants to help bridge political division in the country.

statements.quote: The Environment taking care of the natural resources and contributing to helping move forward with innovation renewable resources and recusing the carbon footprint of the United States.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: Making health care more available and cost less. People should be able to go to the Doctors office for treatments and not worry about how to pay for treatment.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

researchNotes: Dylan Castillo has no campaign website found; his statements come from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Amanda Hollowell's and Jim Kingston's are from their campaign sites. Biography gaps: Hollowell has no campaign-site biography loaded, so her bio relies on her Ballotpedia survey and profile; Kingston's campaign site does not give his birth year, and the Ballotpedia profile for him holds no biography. Ballotpedia lists Dylan Castillo as having 'did not make the ballot' for the Nov. 3 general election, so his ballot status should be verified.
